<div class="course-index course-subpage">
  <a class="course-back-link" href="../index.html">← All neutrino physics materials</a>
  <a class="course-back-link" href="https://neutrinohit.github.io/en/education.html#oscillations-minicourse">NeutrinoHit map card</a>

  <section class="course-intro">
    <p class="course-kicker">Mini-course · English · three lectures</p>
    <h1>Neutrino Oscillations: from Vacuum to the Earth's Core</h1>
    <p>
      Three lectures (about 2 h 45 min) for students of particle physics and
      geophysics. The emphasis is on understanding and on the size of the
      effects: why a neutrino changes flavor, why matter changes the clock,
      and how neutrinos can weigh the Earth, probe the electrons of its core
      and measure its radioactive heat. Interactive applets and animations
      accompany every step.
    </p>
    <p class="course-author">Dmitry V. Naumov, JINR Dubna · <a href="https://neutrinohit.github.io/">neutrinohit.github.io</a></p>
  </section>

  <section class="course-accordion" aria-label="Lectures of the mini-course">
    <details class="course-row" open>
      <summary>
        <span class="course-row-kind">Lecture I</span>
        <span>A Quantum Clock in Vacuum</span>
      </summary>
      <div class="course-row-body">
        <p>
          Ghost particles and the missing solar and atmospheric neutrinos;
          flavor and mass states; beats of two waves; the oscillation formula
          and its two knobs; oscillation lengths and the L/E map; three
          flavors and two clocks.
        </p>
        <div class="course-links">
          <a href="en/slides/01_vacuum.html">Open lecture</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </details>

    <details class="course-row">
      <summary>
        <span class="course-row-kind">Lecture II</span>
        <span>Matter and the Sun</span>
      </summary>
      <div class="course-row-body">
        <p>
          Refraction of neutrinos and the potential of electrons; the MSW
          resonance; slowly changing density; the Sun as a flavor converter;
          the day–night effect; how matter on long baselines reveals the
          neutrino mass ordering.
        </p>
        <div class="course-links">
          <a href="en/slides/02_matter_sun.html">Open lecture</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </details>

    <details class="course-row">
      <summary>
        <span class="course-row-kind">Lecture III</span>
        <span>The Earth Seen by Neutrinos</span>
      </summary>
      <div class="course-row-body">
        <p>
          What seismology knows and what it cannot tell; electrons per nucleon;
          absorption tomography and the mass of the Earth; oscillation
          tomography of the core; geoneutrinos and the Earth's heat budget.
        </p>
        <div class="course-links">
          <a href="en/slides/03_earth.html">Open lecture</a>
        </div>
      </div>
    </details>

    <details class="course-row">
      <summary>
        <span class="course-row-kind">Applets</span>
        <span>Interactive material inside the lectures</span>
      </summary>
      <div class="course-row-body">
        <p>
          Two-flavor laboratory, coupled pendulums, three-flavor triangle and
          probabilities (Lecture I); refraction layers, constant-density and
          adiabatic matter laboratories, long-baseline laboratory (Lecture II);
          a neutrino crossing the Earth, the Earth path explorer and the
          oscillogram laboratory (Lecture III). All calculations run in the
          browser.
        </p>
      </div>
    </details>
  </section>
</div>
